findings.title: Protecting Firefox users following the compromise of eMudhra intermediate certificates
findings.summary_md: Mozilla received a report on Saturday, October 17, 2026 at 20:06 UTC that private keys associated with eight eMudhra intermediate certificates had been compromised. The keys could allow attackers to issue fraudulent certificates, and Mozilla blocked the affected intermediates through Firefox's OneCRL.

findings.title: 8 eMudhra certificates are compromised. Here's what you need to know
findings.summary_md: Cloudflare became aware on October 19, 2026 at approximately 17:00 UTC that private keys associated with eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised. The certificates were widely trusted, prompting emergency blocks across browsers and trust stores.

findings.title: eMudhra Statement on Recent Certificate Security Incident
findings.summary_md: eMudhra's statement, dated October 20, 2026, acknowledged the compromise of eight intermediate certificates and confirmed that Mozilla received the initial report on October 17, 2026 at 20:06 UTC. The company stated it revoked the compromised certificates and stopped issuing new certificates under its G3 root.

findings.title: Indian certification authority eMudhra's private keys compromised
findings.summary_md: The Register reported that eight eMudhra intermediate certificate private keys were compromised, including keys as weak as single-digit integers, reducing 384-bit entropy to 3-8 bits. The incident prompted emergency browser and operating system blocks and distribution updates such as Debian DSA-6572-1.
